searchText: it's useful for wallets to prove data from third-party services, ie when they give you a balance etc, can be done against the light client protocol - so "human response time"? That can be 1s/5s/400ms. Human response time is more close to 10mins or whatever that means ( not sure) I am talking about historical getProofs I dont see any reason why a wallet would want to back in time 10k blocks and prove a storage slot Anyway "latest" is easily sub-second I think what he meant is, the human limit of it feeling instant. This is typically defined to be <= 0.1s https://www.nngroup.com/articles/response-times-3-important-limits/ So the idea would be, when the wallet queries your latest balance, the whole round trip should be below 0.1s, so they don't need to show a loading animation there. Whereas it may be acceptable to have a 'loading' process for historical balance yes - i see. i am talking about historical ones. wallets do not need historical getProofs. i know L2s do need those tho, not sure what is acceptable Subsecond would be ideal - timeouts of 10s per request are pretty typical and anything over a minute gets very hard to handle. If you look at requesting data for fault dispute games you may be making quite a lot of calls for blocks up to 30 days old (games will have resolved before then but you don’t want to stop monitoring games the instant they resolve as the idea is to pick up if they resolved incorrectly or if there was some kind of anomaly). If each call takes a long time you either need to be able to make a ton of them in parallel or monitoring cycles take forever.

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content:
Subsecond would be ideal - timeouts of 10s per request are pretty typical and anything over a minute gets very hard to handle. 
If you look at requesting data for fault dispute games you may be making quite a lot of calls for blocks up to 30 days old (games will have resolved before then but you don’t want to stop monitoring games the instant they resolve as the idea is to pick up if they resolved incorrectly or if there was some kind of anomaly). If each call takes a long time you either need to be able to make a ton of them in parallel or monitoring cycles take forever.
